hook: This is a quiet, melancholy entry rather than a frightening one. The entity at its center takes the place of people who have just died, and the file cares far more about what that is like than about how it works. Expect a short character study dressed up as a containment report, with suicide as one of its subjects.
whyItMatters: Carrying the featured tag in Series I, it shows that the Foundation format can hold grief and identity as easily as horror. Its subject is technically Safe, yet the procedures read like a careful effort to keep someone stable and protected from despair. The humanoid comes across less as a threat to lock away than as someone trapped inside a role it never chose.
thingsToNotice:
The origin hides a double replacement: the real firefighter John died in the first blaze and SCP-069 walked out wearing his life, then three weeks later it went into a smoky room alone and, by every implication, died there and resurfaced as the one civilian who came out almost untouched. It keeps no memory of earlier lives, so each identity feels fully its own, and the urge to settle debts, visit relatives and rewrite wills reads like someone preparing the dead person's family for a loss that has already happened.

It is now living as a guard who was killed during another object's breach, and it first refused to accept what it was. The Foundation briefly considered handing it more dead staff as future identities, which treats a grieving person as a reusable tool. When a junior researcher let slip that the agent's family had been told he was dead and described how they took it, SCP-069 tried to kill itself. The procedures' cold note that it must not be treated as an employee, and the two-officer sign-off on every request, are what that suicide attempt left behind.
